Norway’s Lærdal Tunnel is the longest road tunnel in the world at 24.51 km (15.2 mi), but China’s Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, opened in December 2025, is close behind at 22.13 km. These are 14 road tunnels open to traffic, ranked by length as of October 2026.
**Pictured:** a still from the Norwegian Public Roads Administration film “The Lærdal Tunnel” (uploaded to YouTube by Svein Olav Haukedal); the Lærdal Tunnel is #1, at 24.51 km.

| 2 | Tianshan Shengli Tunnel | 22.13 | China | 2025 | Mountain | 2 tubes | G0711 Ürümqi–Yuli Expressway, Xinjiang; opened 26 December 2025 |  
| 3 | Yamate Tunnel | 18.20 | Japan | 2015 | Urban | 2 tubes, 2 lanes each way | Tokyo Central Circular Route (C2), about 30 m under Yamate Street; first section opened 2007, full length 2015 |  
| 4 | Zhongnanshan Tunnel | 18.04 | China | 2007 | Mountain | 2 tubes | G65 Baotou–Maoming Expressway, Qinling Mountains, Shaanxi |

| 10 | Zigana Tunnel | 14.48 | Turkey | 2023 | Mountain | 2 tubes | D885 near Torul and Maçka; opened 3 May 2023 |  
| 11 | Ryfylke Tunnel | 14.46 | Norway | 2019 | Subsea | 2 tubes | Hundvåg (Stavanger) to Solbakk (Strand), up to 292 m below sea level; the longest subsea road tunnel |  
| 12 | Ovit Tunnel | 14.35 | Turkey | 2018 | Mountain | 2 tubes | D925 between İkizdere and İspir; includes 1.37 km of cut-and-cover avalanche tunnel |

**Read this first:** this ranks road tunnels that are open to traffic as of 22 October 2026, by length portal to portal, to the nearest 10 m. For a twin-tube tunnel the length is that of the longer tube (the two usually differ by a few metres to a few hundred), and a tunnel with one tube for each direction counts once, not as the sum of its tubes. Pilot, service and ventilation tunnels are not counted. Lengths and opening years come from Wikipedia’s “List of longest road tunnels”, cross-checked against operator or government figures (the Norwegian Public Roads Administration for Lærdal and Ryfylke, Turkey’s General Directorate of Highways for Zigana) and Xinhua, Tunnelbuilder or other press for the rest; where sources disagree it is noted in the table.[1][2] The Jinpingshan figure is 17.54 km in the list but 17.50 km in another Wikipedia list of Chinese tunnels, and the Gotthard is 16.918 km in the list and 16.942 km in its own article. The Zigana (14.476 km in the list, 14.481 km on Wikipedia) and Ryfylke (14.4 km official, 14.459 km in the list) are close, so the order of ranks 10 and 11 could swap under another measurement, as could Ovit’s. Left out: rail, metro and pedestrian tunnels; tunnels under construction, including Norway’s Rogfast (about 26.7 km, not expected before 2031) and China’s Taihangshan Tunnel, whose opening could not be confirmed; and WestConnex in Sydney (22.4 km in the list), because it is a network of linked motorway tunnels opened in stages from 2019 to 2023, not one continuous tunnel. The table stops at 14, as the next tunnels on the list (Dabashan, 13.7 km, and Xishan, 13.65 km, both in China) could not be checked against a second source. “Opened” is the year the full tunnel opened to traffic. Looking for other record structures? See The Longest Bridges in the World and The Tallest Skyscrapers in the World.

## The Top 10
#1

## The Top 10
### Lærdal Tunnel — 24.51 km
The world’s longest road tunnel, on the E16 between Lærdal and Aurland in western Norway, is 24.51 km long. It opened on 27 November 2000 and completed the Oslo–Bergen road with no ferry crossings or winter mountain passes. It has one tube with two lanes and cost about 1.08 billion Norwegian kroner. To ease the monotony of the drive, it has three large caverns lit blue and yellow, like a sunrise, roughly every 6 km. The video is the road administration’s own film.[1][2]
#2

## The Top 10
### Tianshan Shengli Tunnel — 22.13 km
Opened on 26 December 2025 on the G0711 Ürümqi–Yuli Expressway, it is the longest expressway (motorway) tunnel in the world and the second-longest road tunnel overall. It cuts a several-hour drive through the Tianshan Mountains to about 20 minutes, and the Ürümqi–Korla trip from about 7 hours to about 3, according to Xinhua. Builder China Communications Construction Company says it has the deepest vertical ventilation shaft of any highway tunnel. The video is from CGTN.[1][2]
#3

## The Top 10
### Yamate Tunnel — 18.20 km
The longest road tunnel in Japan and the longest urban one on this list carries the Central Circular Route (C2) of Tokyo’s Shuto Expressway under Yamate Street, about 30 m down, with two lanes in each direction. The first section opened in December 2007 and the full 18.2 km on 7 March 2015. About 70% was built with shield tunnelling machines. The video, from Metropolitan Expressway Company, explains how drivers evacuate on foot.[1][2]
#4

## The Top 10
### Zhongnanshan Tunnel — 18.04 km
Opened in January 2007 on the G65 Baotou–Maoming Expressway in the Qinling Mountains, south of Xi’an. It has two tubes of about 18 km each and was the longest road tunnel in Asia, and the second-longest in the world, when it opened. Its overburden reaches 1,640 m. No suitable video from an authoritative channel was found, so the icon is shown instead.[1][2]
#5

## The Top 10
### Jinpingshan Tunnel — 17.54 km
Two tubes of about 17.5 km run through Jinping Mountain in Sichuan, linking the sites of the Jinping-I and Jinping-II hydropower stations. Lengths are quoted as 17.50 to 17.54 km. A French-language report puts its deepest point 2,375 m below the surface. Wikipedia lists it as opened in 2011. No suitable video from an authoritative channel was found, so the icon is shown instead.[1]
#6

## The Top 10
### Gotthard Road Tunnel — 16.92 km
On the A2 motorway between Göschenen (Uri) and Airolo (Ticino), it was the longest road tunnel in the world from 1980 until Lærdal opened in 2000. It has one tube with two lanes, with traffic in both directions, a limit of 80 km/h and a drive of about 13 minutes. A second tube is under construction. The video is from the Swiss Federal Roads Office (ASTRA) and describes that second tube.[1][2]
#7

## The Top 10
### Tiantaishan Tunnel — 15.56 km
On the G85 Yinchuan–Kunming Expressway in the Qinling Mountains of Shaanxi, opened in 2021. A Chinese construction report describes it as a six-lane tunnel in separate tubes, with up to 937 m of rock above it. It was billed as the longest six-lane twin-tube expressway tunnel in the world. No suitable video from an authoritative channel was found, so the icon is shown instead.[1]
#8

## The Top 10
### Daliangshan No. 1 Tunnel — 15.37 km
The longest road tunnel in southwest China, on the S71 Leshan–Xichang Expressway in Sichuan. The expressway section opened on 1 January 2026, although Wikipedia lists the tunnel as 2025. It is the first highway tunnel with a full-length central pilot tunnel, which serves for drainage, escape and ventilation, and it crosses two seismic fault lines. Its tubes are 15.32 and 15.28 km in another Wikipedia list. No suitable video from an authoritative channel was found, so the icon is shown instead.[1][3]
#9

## The Top 10
### Muzhailing Tunnel — 15.23 km
Part of the G75 Lanzhou–Haikou Expressway in Gansu, built from 2016 and opened in 2024. Its left tube is 15,226 m and its right tube 15,160 m. No suitable video from an authoritative channel was found, so the icon is shown instead.[1]
#10

## The Top 10
### Zigana Tunnel — 14.48 km
Turkey’s longest tunnel carries the D885 under the Zigana Pass between Torul and Maçka and opened on 3 May 2023. The General Directorate of Highways calls it the longest twin-tube road tunnel in Europe and gives 15.1 km when its connecting roads are included; the tunnel proper is about 14.5 km. It shortened the route by about 8 km. The video is from the Directorate.[1][2]

1.   Wikipedia, List of longest road tunnels (lengths, opening years, tube counts and the left/right tube lengths), read 22 October 2026, with the articles on the Lærdal, Yamate, Gotthard, Ovit, Arlberg and Rogfast projects and List of long road tunnels in China.

### Lærdal Tunnel — 24.51 km
The world’s longest road tunnel, on the E16 between Lærdal and Aurland in western Norway, is 24.51 km long. It opened on 27 November 2000 and completed the Oslo–Bergen road with no ferry crossings or winter mountain passes. It has one tube with two lanes and cost about 1.08 billion Norwegian kroner. To ease the monotony of the drive, it has three large caverns lit blue and yellow, like a sunrise, roughly every 6 km. The video is the road administration’s own film.[1][2]

Opened on 26 December 2025 on the G0711 Ürümqi–Yuli Expressway, it is the longest expressway (motorway) tunnel in the world and the second-longest road tunnel overall. It cuts a several-hour drive through the Tianshan Mountains to about 20 minutes, and the Ürümqi–Korla trip from about 7 hours to about 3, according to Xinhua. On March 19, the excavation of the main tunnels of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel both exceeded 8 kilometers. At 2:00 AM on April 16, the excavation of the hard rock tunnel boring machine (TBM) central pilot tunnel at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel broke through the 12,000-meter node. On April 20, the cumulative excavation advance of the left main tunnel had reached 8,594 meters, and the right tunnel 8,483 meters, with a combined advance of 17,077 meters, accounting for 77.2% of the overall main tunnel excavation task. This successfully broke through the 17-kilometer mark, holding milestone significance and laying a solid foundation for achieving the breakthrough goal of the left, central, and right tunnels of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway within the year.

Official Breakthrough

On May 12, 2024, the excavation of both the left and right main tunnels of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel broke through the 10,000-meter mark, completing 90% of the main tunnel excavation task. On July 1, the year-to-date advance for the left tunnel and right tunnel was 1,267.6 meters and 1,636.6 meters respectively, representing 68.52% and 77.02% of the annual plan, achieving the goal of "half the time, half the task." On July 31, the cumulative excavation of the left tunnel at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel was 11,086.2 meters, the right tunnel 11,002.7 meters, and the TBM central pilot tunnel 12,264.98 meters. On August 17, for the key project G0711 Route Urumqi-Yuli Expressway Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, the left tunnel had cumulatively completed 9,001 meters, accounting for 81.8% of the total project volume; the right tunnel had cumulatively completed 9,048 meters, accounting for 82.2%. The combined excavation of the left and right tunnels reached 18,049 meters, breaking through the eighteen-kilometer mark.
30

As a crucial controlling project of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway Project, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel not only faced harsh construction conditions but also significant construction risks. The project is located in a high-altitude region with an extremely cold climate, with an annual average temperature of minus 5.4 degrees Celsius and a minimum temperature reaching minus 41.5 degrees Celsius. The highest shaft elevation is 3,623 meters above sea level. In such high-altitude and low-temperature environments, the efficiency of construction machinery is greatly reduced.
79
The geological structure of the Tianshan Mountains is complex, featuring unfavorable conditions such as large deformations in soft rock. The 22.13-kilometer-long tunnel traverses a total of 16 geological fault zones. The project also faced the "four highs" challenges—high in-situ stress, high groundwater pressure, high seismic intensity, and high environmental protection standards. The maximum in-situ stress value within the tunnel construction area reached 21.8 megapascals, over 50 times the bearing capacity of ordinary rock. The maximum burial depth of the tunnel is 1,112.6 meters, and during construction, dangers such as rockburst, high ground temperature, and high-pressure water inflow were highly likely, with destructive force equivalent to a magnitude 4–5 earthquake in severe cases.
79
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel overcame these multiple world-class engineering challenges. It employed the world's first innovative Grouting Method, increasing the advance rate in fault zones to 12 meters per day. Originally scheduled for completion in 10 years, this super project was successfully holed through in just 52 months.
77
Multiple World Records

The construction team of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel obtained a total of 67 invention patents and 156 utility model patents, and compiled 5 construction technical standards and 3 construction technical guidelines, fully demonstrating the technological strength and innovative spirit in China's transportation construction field. Among these, the No. 2 shaft of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is the world's first ultra-large-diameter, deep hard rock shaft excavated in one pass. The Chinese independently developed "Chuangshouhao" large-diameter full-face hard rock vertical shaft boring machine, incorporating advanced technologies such as intelligent drilling and AI algorithms for the vertical guidance system to real-time correct the boring trajectory. It penetrated a 30-meter-thick permafrost layer at an altitude of 3,660 meters and in extreme cold of minus 40 degrees Celsius, excavating to a depth of 707 meters, setting three records for depth, diameter, and altitude.
63
Multiple Innovations
It was the first time the combined technique of "hard rock central pilot tunnel + main tunnel drill and blast method" was used in the field of highway tunnels, adopting the "three tunnels + four shafts" construction method. The three tunnels refer to the left and right main tunnels and the central pilot service tunnel. The four shafts involve excavating four shafts at the top of the tunnel, equivalent to opening four "skylights" above the tunnel, to alleviate ventilation difficulties during the construction of the extra-long tunnel and to meet ventilation and exhaust requirements during later operation.

It was the first time that the major national equipment independently innovated and developed by China, the "Tianshanhao" and "Shenglihao" Hard Rock Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs), undertook the tunneling task. These two boring machines have a excavation diameter of 8.43 meters, a total length of 282 meters, and a weight of approximately 2,000 tons. The central pilot tunnel was constructed using the hard rock TBM, creating auxiliary working faces for the two main tunnels and achieving a "shortening of long tunnel construction." Compared to the traditional Drill and Blast Method, construction efficiency increased by 3 to 5 times, and the construction period was shortened from the conventional 10 years for "two-end boring" construction to just over 4 years. This was an innovation in the construction of extra-long highway tunnels in China. More importantly, this method enables safe, environmentally friendly, and efficient tunneling under various world-class complex strata.
87
It was the first time in China's highway survey and design that horizontal directional drilling was employed for a long-distance bore of 2,271 meters, accurately ascertaining the engineering geological and hydrogeological conditions from the tunnel portal to the F6 (Boluokenu-Aqikekuduk Fault Zone) area. The project organized multiple expert seminars, strengthened scientific research, enhanced safety, environmental protection, quality management, and emergency drills, and fully utilized the integrated technology of "5G + Intelligence + Informatization" to monitor the TBM's boring parameters, detect toxic and harmful gases in the tunnel, and provide disaster warning and monitoring.
87
Value and Significance
Reducing the time required to traverse the Tianshan Mountains
As the "throat" project of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel traverses the central Tianshan Mountains and directly connects the northern and southern parts of Xinjiang. Upon completion, it has broken through the transportation barrier between northern and southern Xinjiang, shortening the travel time between the two regions. Traversing the Tianshan Mountains now takes only about 20 minutes, and the drive between Urumqi and the major city of Korla will be reduced from over 7 hours to about 3 hours.
6
Promoting Economic and Social Development in Northern and Southern Xinjiang

The opening of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel signifies that the tourism spatial structure of Xinjiang will be reshaped in the future. The tunnel will become a crucial transportation corridor for tourism within Xinjiang. Its completion facilitates the flow of people, goods, and materials between northern and southern Xinjiang, promoting the development of tourism and related industries, fostering ethnic cultural integration and unity, and contributing to economic prosperity, social stability, and development. It is of significant importance for advancing the construction of Xinjiang as the Core Area of the Silk Road Economic Belt, promoting the economic and social development of Xinjiang, and exploiting regional advantageous resources.

During the 2026 Spring Festival holiday, Korla received a cumulative total of 528,000 tourist visits, representing a year-on-year increase of 22.07%. This route facilitates economic circulation between northern and southern Xinjiang, serves the westward opening-up and the Belt and Road Initiative, and provides crucial support for the nation's overall development.

Reduction in Logistics Costs
Logistics companies previously transported iron ore from Hejing County in southern Xinjiang to Urumqi in northern Xinjiang by train. The main route involved loading at the Baluntai Station in Hejing County, then detouring through Hejing, marshalling at Yanqi, and proceeding through Yanqi, passing through Hoxut, Yu'ergou, and Turpan before finally reaching Urumqi. Following the opening of the Tianshan Tunnel, logistics costs alone are estimated to decrease by approximately 70 million yuan.

In December 2025, the documentary "Tianshan Thoroughfare" aired on CCTV-2 (Finance Channel).

After nearly five years, during which thousands of workers toiled in the heart of the Tianshan Mountains, it stands as another magnificent achievement in China's expressway tunnel construction, following the Qinling Zhongnanshan Tunnel. By TBM Staff January 14, 2025
_Tianshan Mountains in Northwest China (Photo: Dreamstime)._
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, located in the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in Northwest China, completed tunneling on Dec. 30, according to gov.cn.
The tunnel is 22.13-km long and is expected to reduce travel times in the Tianshan Mountains from about three hours to about 20 minutes. When it opens to traffic in 2025, the tunnel will connect the northern and southern sections of the autonomous region.
The length of the tunnel puts it among the longest road tunnels in the world, with gov.cn reporting that it is the world’s longest “expressway tunnel.”
According to the website, tunnel construction began in April 2020. Challenges included “extreme cold, high altitudes, high ground stress, strong seismic activity and strict environmental requirements.” In all, the alignment crossed 16 fault zones.

It was the first time in China's highway survey and design that horizontal directional drilling was employed for a long-distance bore of 2,271 meters, accurately ascertaining the engineering geological and hydrogeological conditions from the tunnel portal to the F6 (Boluokenu-Aqikekuduk Fault Zone) area. The project organized multiple expert seminars, strengthened scientific research, enhanced safety, environmental protection, quality management, and emergency drills, and fully utilized the integrated technology of "5G + Intelligence + Informatization" to monitor the TBM's boring parameters, detect toxic and harmful gases in the tunnel, and provide disaster warning and monitoring.
87
Value and Significance
Reducing the time required to traverse the Tianshan Mountains
As the "throat" project of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel traverses the central Tianshan Mountains and directly connects the northern and southern parts of Xinjiang. Upon completion, it has broken through the transportation barrier between northern and southern Xinjiang, shortening the travel time between the two regions. Traversing the Tianshan Mountains now takes only about 20 minutes, and the drive between Urumqi and the major city of Korla will be reduced from over 7 hours to about 3 hours.
6
Promoting Economic and Social Development in Northern and Southern Xinjiang
texts.17:
The opening of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel signifies that the tourism spatial structure of Xinjiang will be reshaped in the future. The tunnel will become a crucial transportation corridor for tourism within Xinjiang. Its completion facilitates the flow of people, goods, and materials between northern and southern Xinjiang, promoting the development of tourism and related industries, fostering ethnic cultural integration and unity, and contributing to economic prosperity, social stability, and development. It is of significant importance for advancing the construction of Xinjiang as the Core Area of the Silk Road Economic Belt, promoting the economic and social development of Xinjiang, and exploiting regional advantageous resources.
20
During the 2026 Spring Festival holiday, Korla received a cumulative total of 528,000 tourist visits, representing a year-on-year increase of 22.07%. This route facilitates economic circulation between northern and southern Xinjiang, serves the westward opening-up and the Belt and Road Initiative, and provides crucial support for the nation's overall development.
88
Reduction in Logistics Costs
Logistics companies previously transported iron ore from Hejing County in southern Xinjiang to Urumqi in northern Xinjiang by train. The main route involved loading at the Baluntai Station in Hejing County, then detouring through Hejing, marshalling at Yanqi, and proceeding through Yanqi, passing through Hoxut, Yu'ergou, and Turpan before finally reaching Urumqi. Following the opening of the Tianshan Tunnel, logistics costs alone are estimated to decrease by approximately 70 million yuan.
45
Related Works
In December 2025, the documentary "Tianshan Thoroughfare" aired on CCTV-2 (Finance Channel).
63
Social Honors
In January 2026, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel was awarded the title of "World's Longest Highway Tunnel" for its single-bore length of 22.13 kilometers and received official certification from Guinness World Records.
73
Social Evaluation
texts.18:
As the "throat" project of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway in Xinjiang, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel began construction in April 2020. After nearly five years, during which thousands of workers toiled in the heart of the Tianshan Mountains, it stands as another magnificent achievement in China's expressway tunnel construction, following the Qinling Zhongnanshan Tunnel. Once the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel opens to traffic, traversing the formidable Tianshan mountain range that separates northern and southern Xinjiang will take just over 20 minutes. (China Government Network Review)
86
Despite an average altitude of around 3,000 meters and winter outdoor temperatures dropping as low as -20°C, driving inside the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel feels warm, spacious, and swift. In the future, further additions of lighting, ventilation, network coverage, and interior decoration will undoubtedly enhance the driving and riding experience. (Xinjiang Daily Review)
80
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, located deep within the Tianshan Mountains in Xinjiang, is a crucial component of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway. The tunnel continuously traverses 16 geological fault zones and one altered rock zone, with a maximum overburden exceeding 1,112.6 meters. The construction environment combined ultra-high ground stress, extremely cold climate, high-altitude oxygen deficiency, and high seismic activity, earning it the description of a "geological museum" for world-class tunnel engineering. (China Communications Construction Group Official Account Review)
73

In 2026, when Dilinuer Tuerxunjiang, a Xinjiang tour guide, was returning to Urumqi with Ms. Lin's family, a group of tourists from Taiwan, after concluding their tour, they passed through the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel. She provided a detailed introduction to this mega-project: deep within the Tianshan Mountains at an altitude exceeding 3,000 meters, the Chinese literally bored through 22.13 kilometers of the mountain's core to create the world's longest highway tunnel—the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel. It's not that piercing through the Tianshan is easy, but rather that there are people on the other side of the mountains." Dilinuer's heartfelt words quickly made the video go viral online. In October 2025, moved by the beautiful scenery and warm hospitality shared by Dilinuer on social media, Ms. Lin's family traveled to Xinjiang. Dilinuer's family prepared a large table full of local delicacies, deeply touching Ms. Lin's family. "Coming here feels just like being at our own home," they said. This mutual affection and closeness represent a two-way journey between the two families, as well as the profound bond and shared aspiration of compatriots on both sides of the strait, who share the same roots, language, culture, and bloodline.

"Five highs" refer to high in-situ stress, high seismic intensity, high environmental protection requirements, severe cold, and high altitude. Among these, the maximum in-situ stress value in the construction section reaches 21.8 MPa, equivalent to a rock sample the size of a human fingernail bearing a weight of 218 kilograms, exceeding the bearing capacity of ordinary rock by more than 50 times. This means rockbursts are highly likely during construction, generating vibration amplitudes comparable to a magnitude 4-5 earthquake. Furthermore, the geological tectonic activity in the construction area itself is relatively intense, with a basic seismic intensity of VIII.
24
Tunnel Design
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is designed as a separated, bidirectional four-lane expressway tunnel, with a design speed of 100 kilometers per hour.
66
Construction Philosophy
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is adjacent to National Glacier No. 1, situated on the banks of the Urumqi River, in a severely cold, high-altitude uninhabited area with a fragile ecological environment. This region features vast alpine meadows and pristine, rarely visited natural habitats, serving as a paradise for wildlife such as snow leopards, Siberian ibexes, and marmots, as well as rare plants like snow lotus and snow ganoderma. The old National Highway 216 was the only route through the Tianshan Shengli Daban, and the constant flow of tourists and vehicles has caused a certain degree of damage to the local ecological environment.
66
To protect the fragile ecological environment of the project site, the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway project incorporated planning and design from the three stages of engineering feasibility study, construction, and operation, implementing ecological and environmental protection measures concurrently with the engineering construction ("Three Simultaneities"). The project integrated ecological and environmental protection concepts into the overall construction plan from the outset, persisting throughout the entire construction process. Extensive work was undertaken in areas such as water source protection, air pollution control, soil and water conservation, wildlife protection, hazardous waste disposal, and energy conservation and consumption reduction. The construction of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel will significantly protect the alpine glaciers and the plant and animal ecosystems.
66
Technical Solution

Therefore, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel adopted the world's first "three tunnels + four shafts" construction scheme. The "three tunnels" refer to the left main bore, the right main bore, and the central service pilot tunnel. The left and right main bores have an excavation diameter of 14 meters, each designed with two lanes. The central service tunnel has a diameter of 8.4 meters and will be used as an emergency and rescue channel in the future, which can prevent vehicle congestion inside the tunnel due to accidents or other reasons. The "four shafts" refer to the excavation of four vertical shafts along the top of the entire tunnel to achieve longitudinal ventilation, functioning as the tunnel's "respiratory system."
67
Based on factors such as the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel's topography, geological characteristics, construction schedule, and post-operation disaster prevention and rescue requirements, the central pilot tunnel was excavated using a Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM), leveraging the TBM's rapid construction capability. This served two purposes: first, to prospect the geology in advance, and second, to provide working faces for the main bores. The two main bores were excavated using the Drill and Blast Method. The combination of these two techniques achieved the goal of "long tunnel, short construction." The monthly advance rate of the TBM is approximately 3 to 10 times that of the traditional drill and blast method. Furthermore, with the two TBMs operating simultaneously from the north and south directions, and then adding auxiliary working faces to the main bores via cross passages, the main bores were effectively segmented for simultaneous operation, thereby significantly shortening the construction period.
67
Construction Equipment
The "Tianshan" TBM and the "Shengli" TBM are tunneling machines specially built by China Communications Construction Company for the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel. These two TBMs have an excavation diameter of 8.43 meters, are 282 meters long each, and weigh approximately 2,000 tons. Using TBMs (Hard Rock Tunnel Boring Machines) for the service tunnel construction reduced the construction period to 72 months.
66
a mountain tunnel constructed using the world's first Grouting Method by a tunnel boring machine

The "Tianshan" TBM and the "Shengli" TBM are equipped with three different tunneling modes and support methods. They can switch between different tunneling modes and support methods based on varying geological conditions. Under favorable surrounding rock conditions, the open-type tunneling mode can be used. In fault zones, weak surrounding rock, or rockburst-prone strata, the single-shield steel formwork with pressure-grouted concrete support tunneling mode can be employed. In extremely fractured zones, sections with large deformation in soft rock, or strong rockburst strata, the single-shield steel segment support tunneling mode can be applied. The latter two modes essentially provide reinforced support treatment for poor ground conditions to ensure the safety of personnel and equipment.
67
Construction Team
The construction of the entrance portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is undertaken by the construction team of China Communications First Highway Engineering Group Co., Ltd.

Construction History
Background
In 2019, the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway connecting Urumqi to Yuli County officially commenced construction. This project is also a pilot project for building a strong transportation nation. The key control project, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, with a total length of 22.11 kilometers, is the world's longest highway tunnel as of that time.
75
The name of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel originates from the Tianshan Shengli Daban (mountain pass) that the tunnel traverses. This area features high altitude, low temperatures, thin air, and complex geological conditions, amplifying ordinary construction challenges severalfold.
75
Commencement of Construction
In April 2020, the construction of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel began.
77
As of June 2021, the cumulative advance of the TBM service tunnel at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel reached 2.6 kilometers, with a monthly average advance of 350 meters, and set a construction record of 500.2 meters of monthly advance. Both the left and right main tunnels had been excavated for 1.2 kilometers.
75

At 2:00 AM on January 5, 2022, the excavation by the "Shengli" TBM in the service tunnel broke through the 5,000-meter mark. In April of the same year, the cumulative excavation of both left and right main tunnels at the entrance portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel surpassed 2 kilometers each. Specifically, the right main tunnel had advanced a cumulative 2,004.5 meters, the left main tunnel 2,109 meters, and the central pilot tunnel 4,561 meters, successfully meeting the quarterly progress target. On December 20 of the same year, the right tunnel at the entrance portal broke through the 4,000-meter mark.
2
Construction personnel commemorating the breakthrough of 5,000 meters in the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel with a celebration photo

On January 20, 2023, the world's first innovative grouting method (TBM) hard rock tunnel boring machines "Tianshan" and "Shengli", independently developed by Zhongjiao Tianhe, broke through within the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, with the overall excavation progress exceeding 70% of the tunnel's total length. On December 5, at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel in Xinjiang, the "Shengli" TBM hard rock tunnel boring machine successfully excavated 11,028 meters, reaching the tunnel's central point. On December 22, the cumulative excavation of the main tunnels at the entrance portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel broke through the 15-kilometer mark. On December 28, the shaft excavation of the 2-2 well in the Urumqi-Yuli Civil Engineering Section 5 was successfully completed.
16

On January 11, 2024, the excavation of the left and right main tunnels at the entrance portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel reached 70% completion, laying a solid foundation for a good start to the project. On February 28, the excavation of the main tunnels broke through 16 kilometers. As of March 1, the cumulative excavation advance of the left tunnel at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel in Xinjiang was 9,148.4 meters, the right tunnel 9,238.3 meters, and the TBM central pilot tunnel 11,733 meters. On March 19, the excavation of the main tunnels of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel both exceeded 8 kilometers. At 2:00 AM on April 16, the excavation of the hard rock tunnel boring machine (TBM) central pilot tunnel at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel broke through the 12,000-meter node. On April 20, the cumulative excavation advance of the left main tunnel had reached 8,594 meters, and the right tunnel 8,483 meters, with a combined advance of 17,077 meters, accounting for 77.2% of the overall main tunnel excavation task. This successfully broke through the 17-kilometer mark, holding milestone significance and laying a solid foundation for achieving the breakthrough goal of the left, central, and right tunnels of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway within the year.
23
Official Breakthrough

On May 12, 2024, the excavation of both the left and right main tunnels of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel broke through the 10,000-meter mark, completing 90% of the main tunnel excavation task. On July 1, the year-to-date advance for the left tunnel and right tunnel was 1,267.6 meters and 1,636.6 meters respectively, representing 68.52% and 77.02% of the annual plan, achieving the goal of "half the time, half the task." On July 31, the cumulative excavation of the left tunnel at the exit portal of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel was 11,086.2 meters, the right tunnel 11,002.7 meters, and the TBM central pilot tunnel 12,264.98 meters. On August 17, for the key project G0711 Route Urumqi-Yuli Expressway Tianshan Shengli Tunnel, the left tunnel had cumulatively completed 9,001 meters, accounting for 81.8% of the total project volume; the right tunnel had cumulatively completed 9,048 meters, accounting for 82.2%. The combined excavation of the left and right tunnels reached 18,049 meters, breaking through the eighteen-kilometer mark.
30

As a crucial controlling project of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway Project, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel not only faced harsh construction conditions but also significant construction risks. The project is located in a high-altitude region with an extremely cold climate, with an annual average temperature of minus 5.4 degrees Celsius and a minimum temperature reaching minus 41.5 degrees Celsius. The highest shaft elevation is 3,623 meters above sea level. In such high-altitude and low-temperature environments, the efficiency of construction machinery is greatly reduced.
79
The geological structure of the Tianshan Mountains is complex, featuring unfavorable conditions such as large deformations in soft rock. The 22.13-kilometer-long tunnel traverses a total of 16 geological fault zones. The project also faced the "four highs" challenges—high in-situ stress, high groundwater pressure, high seismic intensity, and high environmental protection standards. The maximum in-situ stress value within the tunnel construction area reached 21.8 megapascals, over 50 times the bearing capacity of ordinary rock. The maximum burial depth of the tunnel is 1,112.6 meters, and during construction, dangers such as rockburst, high ground temperature, and high-pressure water inflow were highly likely, with destructive force equivalent to a magnitude 4–5 earthquake in severe cases.
79
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel overcame these multiple world-class engineering challenges. It employed the world's first innovative Grouting Method, increasing the advance rate in fault zones to 12 meters per day. Originally scheduled for completion in 10 years, this super project was successfully holed through in just 52 months.
77
Multiple World Records

The construction team of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel obtained a total of 67 invention patents and 156 utility model patents, and compiled 5 construction technical standards and 3 construction technical guidelines, fully demonstrating the technological strength and innovative spirit in China's transportation construction field. Among these, the No. 2 shaft of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is the world's first ultra-large-diameter, deep hard rock shaft excavated in one pass. The Chinese independently developed "Chuangshouhao" large-diameter full-face hard rock vertical shaft boring machine, incorporating advanced technologies such as intelligent drilling and AI algorithms for the vertical guidance system to real-time correct the boring trajectory. It penetrated a 30-meter-thick permafrost layer at an altitude of 3,660 meters and in extreme cold of minus 40 degrees Celsius, excavating to a depth of 707 meters, setting three records for depth, diameter, and altitude.
63

It was the first time the combined technique of "hard rock central pilot tunnel + main tunnel drill and blast method" was used in the field of highway tunnels, adopting the "three tunnels + four shafts" construction method. The three tunnels refer to the left and right main tunnels and the central pilot service tunnel. The four shafts involve excavating four shafts at the top of the tunnel, equivalent to opening four "skylights" above the tunnel, to alleviate ventilation difficulties during the construction of the extra-long tunnel and to meet ventilation and exhaust requirements during later operation.

It was the first time that the major national equipment independently innovated and developed by China, the "Tianshanhao" and "Shenglihao" Hard Rock Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs), undertook the tunneling task. These two boring machines have a excavation diameter of 8.43 meters, a total length of 282 meters, and a weight of approximately 2,000 tons. The central pilot tunnel was constructed using the hard rock TBM, creating auxiliary working faces for the two main tunnels and achieving a "shortening of long tunnel construction." Compared to the traditional Drill and Blast Method, construction efficiency increased by 3 to 5 times, and the construction period was shortened from the conventional 10 years for "two-end boring" construction to just over 4 years. This was an innovation in the construction of extra-long highway tunnels in China. More importantly, this method enables safe, environmentally friendly, and efficient tunneling under various world-class complex strata.
87

87

Reducing the time required to traverse the Tianshan Mountains
As the "throat" project of the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel traverses the central Tianshan Mountains and directly connects the northern and southern parts of Xinjiang. Upon completion, it has broken through the transportation barrier between northern and southern Xinjiang, shortening the travel time between the two regions. Traversing the Tianshan Mountains now takes only about 20 minutes, and the drive between Urumqi and the major city of Korla will be reduced from over 7 hours to about 3 hours.
6

"Five highs" refer to high in-situ stress, high seismic intensity, high environmental protection requirements, severe cold, and high altitude. Among these, the maximum in-situ stress value in the construction section reaches 21.8 MPa, equivalent to a rock sample the size of a human fingernail bearing a weight of 218 kilograms, exceeding the bearing capacity of ordinary rock by more than 50 times. Tunnel Design
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is designed as a separated, bidirectional four-lane expressway tunnel, with a design speed of 100 kilometers per hour.
66
Construction Philosophy
The Tianshan Shengli Tunnel is adjacent to National Glacier No. 1, situated on the banks of the Urumqi River, in a severely cold, high-altitude uninhabited area with a fragile ecological environment. This region features vast alpine meadows and pristine, rarely visited natural habitats, serving as a paradise for wildlife such as snow leopards, Siberian ibexes, and marmots, as well as rare plants like snow lotus and snow ganoderma. The old National Highway 216 was the only route through the Tianshan Shengli Daban, and the constant flow of tourists and vehicles has caused a certain degree of damage to the local ecological environment.
66
To protect the fragile ecological environment of the project site, the Urumqi-Yuli Expressway project incorporated planning and design from the three stages of engineering feasibility study, construction, and operation, implementing ecological and environmental protection measures concurrently with the engineering construction ("Three Simultaneities"). The project integrated ecological and environmental protection concepts into the overall construction plan from the outset, persisting throughout the entire construction process. Extensive work was undertaken in areas such as water source protection, air pollution control, soil and water conservation, wildlife protection, hazardous waste disposal, and energy conservation and consumption reduction. The construction of the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel will significantly protect the alpine glaciers and the plant and animal ecosystems.

Technical Solution
texts.4:
Therefore, the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel adopted the world's first "three tunnels + four shafts" construction scheme. The "three tunnels" refer to the left main bore, the right main bore, and the central service pilot tunnel. The left and right main bores have an excavation diameter of 14 meters, each designed with two lanes. The central service tunnel has a diameter of 8.4 meters and will be used as an emergency and rescue channel in the future, which can prevent vehicle congestion inside the tunnel due to accidents or other reasons. The "four shafts" refer to the excavation of four vertical shafts along the top of the entire tunnel to achieve longitudinal ventilation, functioning as the tunnel's "respiratory system."
67
Based on factors such as the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel's topography, geological characteristics, construction schedule, and post-operation disaster prevention and rescue requirements, the central pilot tunnel was excavated using a Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM), leveraging the TBM's rapid construction capability. This served two purposes: first, to prospect the geology in advance, and second, to provide working faces for the main bores. The two main bores were excavated using the Drill and Blast Method. The combination of these two techniques achieved the goal of "long tunnel, short construction." The monthly advance rate of the TBM is approximately 3 to 10 times that of the traditional drill and blast method. Furthermore, with the two TBMs operating simultaneously from the north and south directions, and then adding auxiliary working faces to the main bores via cross passages, the main bores were effectively segmented for simultaneous operation, thereby significantly shortening the construction period.

Construction Equipment
The "Tianshan" TBM and the "Shengli" TBM are tunneling machines specially built by China Communications Construction Company for the Tianshan Shengli Tunnel. These two TBMs have an excavation diameter of 8.43 meters, are 282 meters long each, and weigh approximately 2,000 tons. Using TBMs (Hard Rock Tunnel Boring Machines) for the service tunnel construction reduced the construction period to 72 months.
